title: Generated host ownership and pending journals require this release for cleanup
summary: The projection ownership state keeps its format name, ia.host-projection-state.v1, and now lists the generated agent and skill files beside the packet's, and .claude/settings.local.json holds one IA hook group per authored `@hook`, owned through .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json. A published 2.0.0 @inventarch/cli or @inventarch/distribution on such a workspace: every `ia host claude` plan, apply or removal, `ia project claude` and the install refresh first look for IA guard groups, recognize each hook group by its launcher's guard arguments, find no 2.0.0 guard ownership state for it, and refuse with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION ("An IA guard group has no matching ownership state; remove only that guard group before retiring steward files"), which asks the user to delete IA's own group by hand; a state that lists a generated skill (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is refused as an invalid projection ownership state (IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID), for codex too; a claude state that lists generated agents and no skill reads each agent as a 1.x steward file and deletes it as legacy. Interrupted applies are refused too: while a hook registration is interrupted, guard-pending.json holds format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1, so 2.0.0 refuses host writes with IA-DIST-RECOVERY-REQUIRED and its `ia recover guard` refuses the journal as an unknown guard recovery format; and an interrupted projection apply leaves pending receipt evidence (<host>-receipt-pending.json) that may list a generated skill's removal or carry removedHooks, which 2.0.0 refuses as invalid evidence (a generated agent's removal passes its check, which admits agent paths), even for its own `--remove`. This release finishes both: `ia recover guard` for the journal, and its next `ia host <host> --apply` for the evidence. Ownership format trade-off: the state format name is kept rather than bumped. A new name only when generated paths are listed would turn 2.0.0's silent deletion of generated agents into a refusal, but it would also make 2.0.0 refuse every workspace this release applied a generated set to, and the hook groups, which that state does not hold, refuse in 2.0.0 either way. The deletion is accepted because a generated agent is regenerated from its record by this release's next apply. Host cleanup uses this release: finish a pending `.ia/distributions/hosts/guard-pending.json` with `ia recover guard` and pending projection receipt evidence with `ia host <host> --apply`, then remove registered host sets with `ia host claude --remove --apply --yes` and, where registered, `ia host codex --remove --apply --yes`. Unreadable ownership requires the located manual repair first; cleanup never authorizes deleting foreign state. Host removal alone does not make a workspace readable by 2.0.0: initialization with --apply and every applied install, update or remove, including an applied no-op update, activate an engine 0.1.1 lock that the old engine 0.1.0 CLI refuses. Downgrade requires a complete compatible pre-upgrade workspace/state backup, its exact archives and the matching old CLI; do not edit an engine marker. Only after restoring that compatible state may the old CLI register its own host set. A workspace that authors no `@agent-profile`, `@playbook` or `@hook` gets no generated file or hook group written, so its projection and hook shapes stay readable by 2.0.0 when the installation lock and archives are also compatible; its receipt only gains optional sections, which 2.0.0's reader ignores.
